chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Husayn ibn Musa, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) married the slave-wife of his uncle, al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and married his mother to his (freed) slave. When that reached Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, he wrote to him: 'O Ali ibn al-Husayn, it seems you do not know your position among your people and your station among the people! You married a slave woman and married your slave to your mother?' So Ali ibn al-Husayn wrote back to him: 'I understood your letter, and our exemplar is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He married off his cousin Zaynab to his slave Zayd, and he himself married his slave maiden Safiyyah bint Hayy ibn Akhṭab.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Slave woman who bore her master's child
key_terms.زَيْدٌ: Zayd ibn Harithah (the Prophet's freed slave)
key_terms.زَيْنَبُ بِنْتُ عَمِّهِ: Zaynab bint Abi al-As (the Prophet's cousin)
key_terms.عَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ: Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, Umayyad Caliph

ai.seo_question: Why did Ali ibn al-Husayn marry his mother to a slave and what was his justification?
ai.summary: This narrative highlights the Umayyad critique of Ali ibn al-Husayn’s social flexibility, where he married the slave-wife of his uncle al-Hasan and freed his mother to marry her to a former slave. Ali’s response invokes the Prophetic precedent of Zayd ibn Harithah and Safiyyah bint Huyayy to demonstrate that nobility in Islam is defined by piety and lineage rather than rigid class distinctions, a key theme in Shia scholarship regarding the Ahl al-Bayt's adherence to the Sunnah.
